hints: Hint 1: Ask yourself what active transport needs that only a living, respiring cell can supply, and what happens when oxygen runs low.
Hint 2: Remember where ATP is made and which cells do a lot of active transport for translocation, then check if each statement 1, 2 and 3 fits that link.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Recall the energy link**
Active transport moves molecules against a concentration gradient, so it needs energy. That energy comes directly from ATP made in respiration.

Step 2: **Test each observation**
Statement 1 fits because only living cells respire to make ATP. Statement 2 fits because low oxygen slows aerobic respiration, so less ATP is made and active uptake slows. Statement 3 fits because companion cells actively load sucrose into phloem, so lots of mitochondria means lots of ATP supply.

Step 3: **Put it together**
All three observations point to the same idea: no ATP production, no active transport. So 1, 2 and 3 all support the link.

options.A: Correct, as all three statements link active transport to living cells, oxygen for aerobic respiration, and mitochondria for ATP production.
options.B: Incomplete, as it leaves out statement 3 which is strong evidence since companion cells need ATP for active loading.
options.C: Incomplete, as it leaves out statement 1 which is valid because dead cells cannot respire to supply ATP.
options.D: Incomplete, as statements 1 and 2 also support the link, not just statement 3 alone.
